convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom indicator 'i-BandsPrice' with custom smoothing methods (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) from external SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, plus custom trade management from TradeAlgorithms.mqh. The indicator is not a built-in MT5 indicator and the custom smoothing algorithms have no Python equivalents without manual reimplementation.

derived_values.name: min_rates_total - minimum bars before indicator is valid
TimeShiftSec - time offset for signal timestamp
Value[2] - indicator buffer 1 values at SignalBar and SignalBar+1

other_exits: Close buy when indicator buffer value < 2 (crosses below threshold 2)
Close sell when indicator buffer value > 1 (crosses above threshold 1)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MMMode enum selects sizing method: LOT=fixed lot, FREEMARGIN=free margin fraction, BALANCE=balance fraction, LOSSFREEMARGIN=loss-free-margin fraction, LOSSBALANCE=loss-balance fraction. MM=0.1 serves as either lot size or fraction depending on MMMode.

custom_logic_notes: Entry uses discrete state values from i-BandsPrice indicator buffer 1: value==4 then falling below 4 triggers buy; value==0 then rising above 0 triggers sell. Exit uses threshold crossings: buy closes when value<2, sell closes when value>1. The indicator buffer appears to encode a state machine with values 0-4 representing price position relative to Bollinger Bands. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose input booleans act as gate toggles for each signal direction. Recount flag triggers recalculation on first tick or after CopyBuffer failure. GlobalVariableDel_ cleanup on deinit suggests persistent state across restarts.
python_conversion_notes: The i-BandsPrice custom indicator must be reimplemented in Python. It combines Bollinger Bands with a custom smoothing algorithm (selected from 10 methods including JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA via SmoothAlgorithms.mqh). The indicator outputs discrete state values (0-4) in buffer 1, not continuous values. SmoothAlgorithms.mqh contains non-standard moving average implementations (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) that have no direct Python library equivalents - each must be ported manually. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose with built-in position management, money management (5 MarginMode variants), and deviation handling - these must be reimplemented. GetStartBars() from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh calculates warmup periods per smoothing method. The CIsNewBar class for new bar detection needs a Python equivalent. The signal logic uses integer state comparisons (==4, <4, ==0, >0, >1, <2) from the indicator buffer, which simplifies rule translation once the indicator is ported. SL/TP of 1000/2000 pips are extremely large (likely points not pips on 5-digit), verify against symbol _Point.
